message:
You are an independent Aperture scene author for a paired exploratory native WebGPU comparison. Work here in the dot cloud only. Correlation: 9a3a2710133afd7f34ebf7e00e142acd563c8eb8aa77852d26c8072ff44f0630. INITIAL TURN IS READ-ONLY: inspect the provided reference and relevant engine APIs, plan the scene, then report ready. Do not create or modify any file, start a render/server, spawn tasks or run write-producing tests until the parent sends a fresh bounded write permit after your exact worker identity is bound. Do not read the other author's output or contact them.
Reference image to inspect: /workspace/scratch/0190a8c72f8a/aperture-recovery-20261002/benchmarks/native-preflight-20261002/preserved-cottage-reference.png. Engine repo is /workspace/scratch/0190a8c72f8a/aperture-recovery-20261002; read AGENTS.md and docs/VISUAL_QUALITY.md. Engine/library/source tree is read-only. Your eventual exclusive output directory is /workspace/scratch/0190a8c72f8a/aperture-cottage-author-a-20261002. Aperture source is the engine bytes at main commit 2c89bd7b1ea6583b990a9745ba9fa4cbf7f28c33; three.js control is exact vendored shadow-lab/src/compare/three.webgpu.js and three.core.js with actual REVISION 185dev, not an assumed release label.
Goal: reproduce the preserved low-poly cottage composition with genuine editable procedural geometry: cream gabled house, orange roof, open doorway and inset window, two tiered evergreen trees, four path slabs, brown bench with separate slats/legs, square green base. Match shape, layout, framing, palette and lighting. No downloaded assets, image textures of the reference, generated meshes or screenshot fakery. Use native engine APIs. Aperture must use its app/ECS facade and real geometry; three.js must use WebGPURenderer and reject WebGL fallback. Plan a clean scene module plus minimal HTML/worker if needed, ready global __COTTAGE_READY__={ok:true,...}, and URL-controlled view=front|rear|side and edit=base|roof|bench|trees. Edits: increase roof ridge height by 30% while keeping eaves fixed; widen bench seat and slats by 25% while preserving leg attachment; move both trees outward along X by 0.6 world units. Export/report deterministic part bounds and parameters for independent checks. Use square 800x800 capture, pixel ratio1, fixed camera per view, neutral background, daylight-style lit materials. No animation or random geometry. Keep alternate views real.
Equal author budget: initial source submission plus at most one revision after seeing your own render; up to 8 retained render attempts per engine (including failures). Render time and blocked waiting are not author implementation credit. Same inherited model and xhigh effort for both authors; exact model ID is not exposed, so no formal scored claim based on unverified model identity. Available visible instructions, source submissions and tool results will be retained; do not provide private reasoning or claim a complete transcript export. Parent handles render permission and publication. First report only API/entrypoint choice, intended files and readiness. Report useful results right away, before scratch notes. If work remains, use collaboration.send_message; otherwise return the result. Keep your status report short; complete the research and deliverable at the depth the task requires. If authorization is missing, or the reviewer denies an action for that reason, pause and report the exact action, target, and blocker to me. If I send <transcript_evidence> that authorizes that action and target, proceed; if already denied, retry the same tool call once. Don’t add the evidence to tool arguments. If the evidence is insufficient or the retry is denied, stop and report back. If you delegate that action, forward the block unchanged.
